input.quote: 5.8.1 Harpoon shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to (a) directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, or (b) license, authorize, appoint, or otherwise enable any Third Party to directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, except, in each case ((a) and (b)), as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement.
input.rationale: The only exclusivity covenant in the Agreement (Section 5.8, p0368-p0369) runs against Harpoon, the counterparty: Harpoon and its Affiliates may not develop, commercialize or enable Third Parties to exploit any Competing Product in the Territory, with only an Acquisition/Change in Control carve-out that requires the acquirer to Segregate the Competing Product and preserves AbbVie's unilateral rights to cut off its Confidential Information and disband the JGC. That is exclusivity in our favour and is expressly acceptable under the rule. Searches for sourcing or non-compete duties on AbbVie ("sole supplier", requirements purchase, "AbbVie shall not", non-compete, supply) return nothing restrictive: to the contrary, AbbVie has the sole right to Manufacture (or have Manufactured) and supply Licensed Compounds and Products (Section 4.5.1, p0340), may appoint distributors and co-promotion partners in its sole discretion (Sections 5.4-5.5, p0360-p0361) and may sublicense through multiple tiers (Section 5.3). The exclusive licences granted to AbbVie at Section 5.1.3 and Harpoon's retained rights at Section 5.6.1 impose no reciprocal sourcing obligation on us. This meets the preferred position (no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Customer); no redline is warranted.

mappings.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
